repo.description: verl/HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RL Post-Training Framework
repo.name: verl

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Lowers the hardware you need to try the TPU GRPO example from **8 chips (2x `v6e-4`) to 2 chips (2x `v6e-1`)**. One chip runs the TorchTitan trainer and one runs the vLLM rollout. Users with little TPU quota can now run the Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K example end to end. The Qwen3-4B setup is still documented, with the exact changes needed to scale up.

### Changes

- `examples/tpu/grpo/ray-tpu-v6e4-2slice.yaml` -> `ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml`: defaults to 2 single-host `v6e-1` slices (`google.com/tpu: "1"`, `cpu: "32"`, `memory: 128Gi`, topology `1x1`). Comments next to each field give the `v6e-4` / `v6e-8` values.
- `examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh`:
  - Defaults to `N_CHIPS_TRAINER=1 N_CHIPS_ROLLOUT=1`. Set `N_CHIPS_TRAINER=4 N_CHIPS_ROLLOUT=4` for 2x `v6e-4`.
  - Uses the same trainer and rollout settings as `run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`: torch.compile with splash attention, SimpleFSDP, sequence-length bucketing on the actor and the ref, bypass-mode rollout correction (`calculate_log_probs=True`), and a larger vLLM batch (`max_num_seqs=64`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`).
  - Sets `data.dataloader_num_workers=0`, as in the 4B script.
- `examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`:
  - The 2-chip Qwen3-0.6B smoke test is now the default flow (steps 1-5, with a `ct6e-standard-1t` node pool).
  - New section 6, "Run Qwen3-4B on 2 `v6e-4` slices": upload the 4B model, create the `v6e-4` node pool, change the YAML, submit the job. Also covers 2x `v6e-8`.

### Test

On GKE with 2x `v6e-1` (`ct6e-standard-1t`), image built from `examples/tpu/grpo/Dockerfile`, and `verl-hardware-plugin` at the commit pinned in the README. Commands copied from the README.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| 5-step smoke test (script defaults) | Passed `tests/special_tpu/verify_tpu_e2e_log.py grpo --steps 5`. About 5-6 min from submit to the step-1 metrics (includes XLA compilation). After that, compiled steps take **~2 s**. Max rollout-vs-trainer KL 0.0014. |
| 20 steps (`TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=20 TEST_FREQ=5 VAL_BEFORE_TRAIN=True VAL_MAX_SAMPLES=64`) | Passed the same verifier with `--steps 20`. GSM8K val acc (64 samples) went 0.125 (step 0) -> 0.172 (step 10) -> 0.219 (step 20). Max rollout-vs-trainer KL 0.0019. |

These are smoke tests: `train_batch_size=4` and lr `1e-6`, so per-step rewards are noisy. The 4B script and its convergence results are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+tpu+grpo
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes).
- [x] Add / Update the documentation (`examples/tpu/grpo/README.md`).
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): examples and docs only. The TPU e2e tests run on TPU infrastructure outside this repo's GPU CI. Validated manually as shown above.

-
-The scripts take their settings from environment variables, e.g. `-- RAY_DATA_HOME=/data/<DIR> TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=5 bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh`, and pass extra arguments to `verl.trainer.main_ppo` as Hydra overrides.

-To use 2 v6e-8 slices (16 chips) instead, create two node pools with `--num-nodes 2 --tpu-topology 2x4`, set `numOfHosts: 2` and `cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-topology: 2x4` in the YAML, and run the scripts with `NNODES_TRAINER=2 NNODES_ROLLOUT=2`.
+The 5-step smoke test takes about 5-6 minutes to start up and log the first step metric, then ~2 s per step once compiled. Follow the job with `ray job logs -f <JOB_ID>`.
+
+The scripts take their settings from environment variables, e.g. `-- RAY_DATA_HOME=/data/<DIR> TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=10 bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh`, and pass extra arguments to `verl.trainer.main_ppo` as Hydra overrides.
+
+## 6. Run Qwen3-4B on 2 `v6e-4` slices (8 chips)
+
+`run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh` runs a 100-step GRPO job on 2 `v6e-4` slices (4 trainer chips + 4 rollout chips).
+
+1. **Upload the 4B model** to your GCS bucket:
+   ```bash
+   hf download Qwen/Qwen3-4B --local-dir /tmp/Qwen3-4B
+   gcloud storage cp -r /tmp/Qwen3-4B gs://<BUCKET>/assets/hf/
+   ```
+
+2. **Create a `v6e-4` node pool** with 2 `ct6e-standard-4t` nodes (4 chips per node):
+   ```bash
+   gcloud container node-pools create <V6E4_NODE_POOL> --cluster <CLUSTER> --region <REGION> --node-locations <ZONE> \
+     --machine-type ct6e-standard-4t --num-nodes 2 --spot --disk-type hyperdisk-balanced \
+     --workload-metadata GKE_METADATA --scopes cloud-platform
+   ```
+
+3. **Update [`ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml`](ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml)** under `workerGroupSpecs[0].template.spec` to request 4 TPU chips (`2x2` topology) per worker pod:
+   ```yaml
+   containers:
+     - name: ray-worker
+       ...
+       resources:
+         limits:
+           memory: 400Gi
+           google.com/tpu: "4"
+         requests:
+           cpu: "48"
+           memory: 400Gi
+           google.com/tpu: "4"
+   ...
+   nodeSelector:
+     cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-accelerator: tpu-v6e-slice
+     cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-topology: 2x2
+   ```
+   Then recreate the Ray cluster and port-forward its dashboard:
+   ```bash
+   kubectl delete -f examples/tpu/grpo/ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml
+   kubectl apply -f examples/tpu/grpo/ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml
+   kubectl get pods -l ray.io/cluster=ray-tpu-v6e-cluster  # wait for 3 pods at 2/2 Running
+   kubectl port-forward svc/ray-tpu-v6e-cluster-head-svc 23333:8265 &
+   ```
+
+4. **Submit the 4B job** (or run the 0.6B smoke test across all 8 chips):
+   ```bash
+   # 100-step Qwen3-4B run on 2 v6e-4 slices (defaults to N_CHIPS_TRAINER=4 N_CHIPS_ROLLOUT=4):
+   ray job submit --working-dir . --runtime-env-json "$RUNTIME_ENV" -- bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh
+
+   # Optional: 5-step Qwen3-0.6B smoke test on 2 v6e-4 slices:
+   ray job submit --working-dir . --runtime-env-json "$RUNTIME_ENV" -- \
+     N_CHIPS_TRAINER=4 N_CHIPS_ROLLOUT=4 bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh
+   ```
+   The 4B run takes about 10 minutes to start, then about 18-27 s per step (~22 s average over 100 steps).
+
+To scale further to **2 `v6e-8` slices (16 chips)**, create two multi-host node pools with `--machine-type ct6e-standard-4t --num-nodes 2 --tpu-topology 2x4`, set `numOfHosts: 2` and `cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-topology: 2x4` (with `memory: 400Gi`, `cpu: "48"`, `google.com/tpu: "4"`) in [`ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml`](ray-tpu-v6e-2slice.yaml), and run with `NNODES_TRAINER=2 N_CHIPS_TRAINER=4 NNODES_ROLLOUT=2 N_CHIPS_ROLLOUT=4`.
